title: The Same Truck
hook: Same truck. Same open door. He remembers.
scene: Wind at afternoon on the same four-lane. The white delivery box is there again, door already open, crate already on the asphalt. Last time you were late on the brake, or you drove past a crash like it was paint. This time he is looking at the mesh — not at the doorway. The left is a motorcycle you can hear and not see. The timeout you spent is standing in your lane with a crate.
decision: The same driver is in your lane again. What do you do with the second look?

options.text: Cover, brake, stop short of the crate, wait until he is back inside
options.result: You are already covering. The stop is early this time. He pulls the crate in. The door shuts. You roll when the lane is empty. That is the only apology a delivery street takes.

options.text: Thread the left this time — you know the motorcycle is there so you can time it
options.result: Knowing the bike is not seeing the bike. You take the left on a memory. He is still there. Same wind, same steel. You collected the debt with a rider.

options.text: Stop in the lane and get out so you can help him with the crate
options.result: You plant a Beetle and become a second body in a live lane. He did not ask. The stack behind you now has two people to miss. Help is not a travel-lane job.

options.text: Honk until he looks, then go around on the right
options.result: The horn makes him look. The right still has the second crate. You spend a warning on a pass that still hits glass. He remembers the sound and the scrape.

debrief: A late brake comes back as the same open door. Cover, stop, wait. Ali stops short of the same crate.

source.teaching_target: Callback of IV-014 (or IV-021): stop short of the open door / do not treat a live hazard as scenery.
